title: Add RAG agent tool-calling quickstarts and docs site updates
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: provide opinionated RAG agent quickstarts demonstrating tool-calling patterns (search, simple database lookups, and external tool execution) to lower friction for customers adopting agents with Redwood. Includes docs site updates to add new Quickstarts section, sidebar nav, code samples in Python/TS, and a small end-to-end integration example.

What this PR does: adds three RAG agent quickstarts (search-backed QA agent, multi-tool orchestration agent, and a safe tool-calling pattern example), updates docs site navigation and includes runnable code snippets and a reproducible sample dataset. Adds lightweight integration tests and CI job to validate example run.

Checklist: [x] Quickstart markdown pages for Python and TypeScript [x] Code samples under redwood-examples/rag-agents [x] Docs site sidebar + breadcrumbs updated [x] Integration test in perf-canary/examples-ci [x] Reviewed and approved by Docs and Platform [x] Add note for private deploys (VPC) about network egress for tool-calls

Testing and validation: local smoke-tested examples (python/ts) against local dev server; CI integration job runs example harness with a mocked search API and verifies tool-call metrics are emitted. Manual review validated API surface and that examples follow recommended pattern for secure tool-calling (least-privilege, input sanitization, and timeout handling).

Migration/rollout: docs site change is additive. No user migrations required. Examples are consumable from redwood-examples with a top-level README explaining environment variables and secrets (KMS note for private deployments).

Related: ENG-4312 (RAG quickstarts backlog), DOCS-78 (site nav restructure). Links: docs quickstart preview: /docs/quickstarts/rag-agents, example repo: redwood-examples/rag-agents.

Notes: kept code examples intentionally small; production guidance included in docs with links to Redwood Optimize for batching/quant recommendations. This is a docs-first effort to reduce support requests for agent onboarding.
